Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Quick context: our security & forensics team is running a SIG/CAIQ review for an upcoming audit and surfaced a blocking requirement: for certain incident investigations they want a 120-day window for ephemeral inference logs (session traces, prompt/response hashes, and debug metadata). OptiHealth does not want full-text prompts retained, we indicated pseudonymization/hashed prompt storage is acceptable, but the auditor has asked for an explicit customer exception from Redwood and evidence of controls.

Can Redwood confirm whether an exception can be made, what compensating controls you can commit to (role-based access, encryption, redaction pipeline), and what evidence we can attach to the SIG response? I attached the SIG worksheet and a short exception request PDF.

We'd like a short mutual action plan so we can include timelines in the audit packet. Our timelines are tight: auditor expects evidence by 2028-07-05.

Thanks,
Alyssa Park
Director, Security Operations
OptiHealth

Thanks Alyssa — appreciate the clear ask and the attachments. Putting internal folks on copy to confirm feasibility and controls. High level thoughts:

- Redwood's default for ephemeral inference/session logs is 30 days. We can consider a customer-scoped exception with strict limitations.
- For auditability we can provide forensic evidence (s3 access logs, retention lifecycle policy snapshots, and redaction pipeline logs) and a signed exception amendment.

Immediate proposals for OptiHealth (draft):
1) Short exception window: 90 days for "session trace" (hashed/pseudonymized prompt + response metadata), 30 days for PII-adjacent logs.
2) Compensating controls: encryption-at-rest (customer-managed KMS option), MFA + restricted IAM roles for any access, mandatory justification and approval workflow for staff access, and full access logging.
3) Evidence bundle: S3 lifecycle policy export, snapshot of retention config, role audit, and a written DPA amendment signed by both parties.

Marissa/Rishi — can you confirm technical and legal constraints? If we can accept 90 days we should draft the DPA amendment and produce the SIG attachments the customer needs. Alyssa — if 90 days is acceptable, we'll put together a MAP and schedule a call to finalize language.

- Steph
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Folks — quick technical note from CS/security eng perspective:

- Types of data: we distinguish (A) inference request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts), (B) session traces (prompt hashes + short response fingerprints), (C) KV cache dumps and model artifacts (never kept long-term by default).
- Implementation for exception: we can enable a customer-scoped lifecycle rule that transitions session traces to a locked, encrypted S3 prefix with an expiring legal hold for X days, then automatic purge. This is straightforward.

Requirements I recommend we insist on from customer:
1) Clear statement they will not store PHI or identifiable patient data in prompts; if they must, we need formal legal signoff and SOC2 scope expansion.
2) Signed Customer Exception Form that lists scopes and expiry.
3) Scoped IAM + just-in-time access (ticketed) for any Redwood engineer who needs to access logs.

Evidence deliverables we can produce for the SIG/CAIQ response: lifecycle policy export, an S3 object listing snapshot, an export of the IAM role audit (last 90 days), and redaction pipeline configuration.

I can assemble those items if legal signs off on the exception terms. Recommended default window = 90 days for session traces only.

— Marissa
Principal, Customer Solutions (Security Liaison)

Thanks — legal/compliance input below. Short version: OK to consider conditional exception but must be documented and timeboxed. Key requirements: 

- DPA amendment referencing the exception and confirming OptiHealth's obligations (no PHI, or if PHI, explicit handling terms).
- Customer must sign an attestation that retained artifacts are pseudonymized and used only for debugging and incident response.
- Add exception to our internal Exceptions Register (with expiry) and require quarterly review by Security.
- No replicated backups outside the scoped prefix; snapshots for legal hold only and under separate approval.

Suggested clause (for drafting team): "Redwood agrees to retain pseudonymized session trace artifacts for a period of 90 days solely for the purposes of debugging and incident investigation. Customer represents and warrants that retained data will not contain unredacted PHI or other regulated data. Access to retained artifacts will be restricted to named Redwood personnel on a just-in-time ticketed basis and will be logged; retention will automatically expire at the end of the 90-day period unless renewed in writing by mutual agreement."

I'll coordinate with Contracts to draft a short amendment; need Ops to confirm technical enforcement and CS to confirm they'd collect the SIG evidence artifacts.

— Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
